direct_answer: Neste states that it "does not have a separate climate transition plan as detailed in the ESRS"; instead, it relies on its "targets, actions, resource plans and internal carbon price" to support climate change mitigation transition [Source 1]. Because a separate ESRS-style transition plan is not in place, Neste does not explicitly confirm that such a transition plan is aligned with limiting global warming to 1.5°C [Source 1]. However, Neste explains that it uses climate frameworks (including SBTi guidance, TPI pathways based on the IEA Net Zero 2050 scenario, and ERI) to guide target development toward 1.5°C pathways, and it considers its Scope 1&2 2030 target to be in line with 1.5°C pathways [Source 3]. On timeline: Neste says it "will evaluate the development of specific climate transition plan" (e.g., to align with the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive), but it does not provide a date or timeframe for adoption [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: The company clearly discloses that it does not have a separate ESRS climate transition plan and describes alternative elements (targets/actions/resources/internal carbon price) intended to support mitigation [Source 1]. It provides partial 1.5°C-related information via its target-setting approach and an explicit statement that its Scope 1&2 2030 target is considered 1.5°C-aligned [Source 3]. However, it does not provide an ESRS E1-1 transition plan with an explanation of overall plan compatibility with 1.5°C, and it does not disclose a concrete timeline for adopting a specific climate transition plan [Source 1].
disclosure_gaps: No separate ESRS E1-1 climate transition plan is provided; disclosure indicates reliance on targets/actions/resources/internal carbon price instead [Source 1].
No explicit statement that a transition plan (as such) is aligned with limiting warming to 1.5°C; only partial target-level 1.5°C alignment is stated (Scope 1&2 2030) [Source 3].
No timeline/date for when Neste will adopt a specific climate transition plan; only that it will evaluate developing one [Source 1].

Insufficient detail (in the provided passages) on whether targets are formally validated as science-based (e.g., SBTi approval status), underlying scenarios for all targets, and whether targets have been externally assured (ESRS E1-4.34(e)) [Source 3].
key_findings: Neste does not have a separate climate transition plan as detailed in ESRS; it states its targets, actions, resource plans and internal carbon price are intended to support mitigation transition [Source 1].
Neste will evaluate developing a specific climate transition plan (e.g., to align with the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive) but provides no adoption date [Source 1].

Neste uses frameworks including SBTi guidance, TPI pathways (based on IEA Net Zero 2050 scenario) and ERI to guide target development toward 1.5°C pathways, and it considers its Scope 1&2 2030 target to be in line with 1.5°C pathways [Source 3].
